items.t: Secondary suites and townhouse suites — Surrey: the City defines a secondary suite as an accessory dwelling unit whose habitable floor area does not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit, within a single family, semi-detached or duplex building, and not a separate strata lot; only one suite is permitted per dwelling unit, and a suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite. Surrey Council has approved bylaw changes to permit secondary (lock-off) suites in townhouses in the RM-15, RM-23 and RM-30 zones for new developments in transit-oriented areas and frequent bus stop areas, with a suite minimum of 30 sq. m and less than 40% of the habitable floor area of the larger principal unit — those permissions are for new developments in specified zones and areas, not a blanket right in a 2011-era complex like Arista.
Property taxes — Surrey: City of Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty if not paid by midnight July 2 and a further 5% penalty after September 2.

Surrey has a new Official Community Plan — June 15, 2026. The Surrey 2050 OCP (Bylaw No. 21900) received final adoption on June 15, 2026 per a City corporate report — any older page or document citing the PlanSurrey 2013 OCP (Bylaw No. 18020) as current for Grandview Heights is out of date.

Grandview's attached pool is the community's second-largest. Grandview carried 146 Condos & Townhomes listings in September 2026, behind only White Rock (193) of 593 community-wide, at a 14% sales ratio. Arista resales are a single-complex subset of that pool, not a board category — there is no Arista row to quote.
The complex has a clubhouse and a guest suite — on the page's word.
An independent school sits in the same pocket.

Surrey's tax deadline is not the usual one buyers expect. City of Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty if not paid by midnight July 2 and a further 5% penalty after September 2 — a completion straddling early July needs the tax position settled on the statement of adjustments.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Arista Townhomes

items.t: Surrey plans: OCP = Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026) — Bylaw No. 18020 is REPLACED and is never cited as current.

SSMUH (Surrey position): zoning changes adopted July 8, 2024 — a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. SSMUH is a fee-simple / small-lot frame; it does not re-subdivide an existing strata complex — an Arista strata lot's density is fixed by its strata plan and zoning, not by SSMUH.

Secondary suites (Bylaw No. 12000): the City defines a secondary suite as an accessory dwelling unit whose habitable floor area does not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit, within a single family, semi-detached or duplex building, and not a separate strata lot; only one suite per dwelling unit, and never within a coach house or garden suite.
Surrey short-term rentals: permitted, owner-only; licence figure carried as $358/yr, with the $350/yr proposal figure disclosed as a conflict.

Strata block — applies to Arista in full (its lot IS a strata lot): Form B diligence (SPA s. 123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions — Arista carries no verified age bylaw and is NOT a 55+ complex in any source checked; a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no ALR parcel is documented for this site): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within the principal residence only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of the land's value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, asserted here only as the standing ledger states it.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Arista Townhomes
Local rules that affect duplexes in Arista Townhomes

items.t: Zoning and plan (Surrey): Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000 governs; the governing OCP is Bylaw 21900 (Surrey 2050, adopted Jun 15, 2026) — Bylaw 18020 is replaced and never cited as current. Which zone permits a two-unit (duplex) form on a given parcel is a parcel-by-parcel read of Bylaw 12000. For Arista itself the governing form is its registered strata townhouse form — a buyer reads the strata plan and bylaws, not a duplex permission.

The City defines a secondary suite as an accessory dwelling unit whose habitable floor area does not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit, within a single family, semi-detached or duplex building, and not a separate strata lot; only one suite is permitted per dwelling unit, and a suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite. Separately, Surrey Council approved bylaw changes to permit secondary (lock-off) suites in townhouses in the RM-15, RM-23 and RM-30 zones for new developments in transit-oriented areas and frequent bus stop areas, with a suite minimum of 30 sq. M and less than 40% of the habitable floor area of the larger principal unit — those townhouse permissions are not a blanket right in a 2011-era complex like Arista; if a lock-off or suite use matters to a purchase there, check the townhouse-suite rules and the strata bylaws first.
